discoveries.headline: What is Q-Day, and why does Bitcoin care?
discoveries.why: Q-Day is the day a quantum computer could break the cryptography that protects Bitcoin. Decrypt's Jason Nelson explains why around 1 million early, Satoshi-era coins are most exposed, and why the fix is hard: post-quantum signatures can be 10 to 100 times larger than today's. A clear way to understand one of crypto's biggest long-term questions. Education, not advice.

discoveries.headline: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as COP31 meets
discoveries.why: As countries meet at COP31 in Antalya, Carbon Brief has added up the money on the table. New public climate-finance pledges to developing countries average about $11.7bn a year for the rest of the decade, down from about $40bn, and only five countries have announced new multi-year pledges. A sober, data-led look at the gap the negotiators are working with.

discoveries.headline: Seahorses, dolphins and surfers at Tamarama
discoveries.why: Julien Anton was named Ocean Photographer of the Year for a black-and-white image of a seahorse with its newborn young in Moorea, French Polynesia. Closer to home, Gergo Rugli won the Adventure category with dolphins riding waves beside surfers at Tamarama Beach in Sydney, and Jenny Stock's sea lion pups in Jurien Bay, WA, helped win her the Female Fifty Fathoms Award. A calm, salty scroll.
discoveries.meta_credit: Colossal · Kate Mothes · Ocean Photographer of the Year

discoveries.headline: A five-minute self-compassion break
discoveries.why: Kristin Neff's Self-Compassion Institute shares 19 recorded guided practices, from under four minutes to just over twenty. Start with the General Self-Compassion Break: 5 minutes 13 seconds that bring kindness to whatever you're struggling with right now. If you have longer, Affectionate Breathing (18 min) is a warm take on a classic breath meditation.

discoveries.headline: Friction-maxxing: is the hard way better?
discoveries.why: Friction-maxxing means deliberately choosing slower, analogue options, like a mental map over GPS or cooking over delivery, to give everyday rituals more meaning. Sana Qadar talks with writer Kathryn Jezer-Morton and University of Toronto psychologist Michael Inzlicht about when effort adds value, and when life is hard enough already. Good company for the commute.
discoveries.source: All in the Mind · ABC Radio National
discoveries.meta_credit: ABC Radio National · All in the Mind · Sana Qadar

discoveries.headline: Shan Turner-Carroll wins the Fisher's Ghost
discoveries.why: Burmese/Australian artist Shan Turner-Carroll has won the $50,000 Fisher's Ghost Art Award with I love You, a work that treats sculpture 'not as representation, but as prayer itself'. This year drew a record number of entries, and it's the last prize before Campbelltown Arts Centre closes for redevelopment. The free exhibition runs in Campbelltown until 4 December.
discoveries.meta_credit: Art Collector · Kaitlin Stewart · Campbelltown Arts Centre

discoveries.headline: What actually slows biological ageing?
discoveries.why: Yale researchers led by Raghav Sehgal and Albert Higgins-Chen pooled 51 clinical studies that tracked epigenetic ageing clocks. Physical activity combined with a healthy eating plan consistently lowered biological age, while over-the-counter supplements showed no measurable effect. They're careful to say a lower clock reading isn't yet proof of a longer life. General information, not medical advice.
discoveries.meta_credit: ScienceDaily · Yale School of Medicine · published in Nature Medicine

discoveries.headline: Ten minutes of chair yoga
discoveries.why: Yoga teacher Dave Rennie from Space to Breathe leads a gentle seated practice for strength, balance and flexibility, with a variation for every posture. All you need is a chair with a back; a cushion and blanket are optional. A perfect movement snack between meetings, and free to watch.
discoveries.source: Royal Voluntary Service · Virtual Village Hall
discoveries.meta_credit: Royal Voluntary Service · Dave Rennie, Space to Breathe

discoveries.headline: Squats, step-ups and press-ups for the long run
discoveries.why: Dr Christopher Hurst of Newcastle University explains why strength training may be one of the best tools we have for healthy ageing, and how little it takes to begin: once or twice a week, starting with squats, step-ups and press-ups. Plain, encouraging and easy to act on.
discoveries.meta_credit: Newcastle University · Dr Christopher Hurst (via The Conversation)
